title: Free at Last
subtitle: Freedom will be yours eventually, but is that truly what's best?

items.speaker: Children
items.text: When black grass creeps, the children cry, a thousand fields where dead ones lie.

items.speaker: Children
items.text: When thunder roars and dark clouds curl, the earth splits wide, the spirits swirl.
Jail, Ancient Zhu County

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm? A local rhyme from Huanzhou, isn't it?
In the cell, Paper Heron listens with interest to the distant children's voices. Her mule chews straw on the floor, unconcerned with their present state of affairs.
Beside her, Mayfly strains on her tiptoes at the small cell window, her face a contortion of overlapping anxieties.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: It's only been a few hours since we came in, and they've already captured another five Yao. We're doomed.
She turns dejectedly and leans against the cell's earthen wall.
After a moment of brooding silence, she yanks the once-cherished object from her pocket and flings it to the ground.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Liar! You wretched, dirty liar!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: That merchant swore his trinket could fool the Reversion Bell, but it didn't. I spent all I had on it.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: And that wretched yellow dog. If it hadn't made such a scene, I might have slipped right past. I hate you. I hate you all!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *sob* I'm such a fool.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Now, now. They'll release us soon. We only need to wait.
Paper Heron smiles, looking first at the distraught Mayfly, then toward the trampled amulet on the floor.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And, for the record, your amulet is not a fake. Its power is merely too weak to silence the Reversion Bell without a spell. It could be that the merchant forgot to tell you.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You're no fool. No one's to blame.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: A-Are you defending him? D-Don't you see how miserable I am?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Now, now, we'll be just fine. They can't keep us locked away forever.
She picks up the amulet while murmuring a few words, then dusts it off, and hands it back to Mayfly.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Here, take this. Might prove useful.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Get that away from me!

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: All right, all right, no need to fear. Remember that spell I cast on you? Now they'll see you as just a bundle of hay. I'll pick you up and take you with me when I'm freed.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *sigh* I never should have come here.
The offer does little to lift her spirits. The grass ornament in her hair droops over, matching her defeated expression.
Paper Heron, by contrast, seems completely unbothered by their predicament. Instead, her eyes are fixed on a stone in the corner of her cell.
A moment passes before she lets out a cry of delight.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: And done!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: W-What?
Paper Heron moves in a flourish, presenting the stone to her companion.
It now bears a carving that reads, "Mayfly and Paper Heron were here."

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Well, there isn't much else to do cooped up in here. How do you like it, eh?
Mayfly looks at the stone brick still dusted with debris. The grooves of the carving match the width of Paper Heron's finger.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Did you carve that with your nails?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Haha, no. Just a little trick I picked up on the road—carving with air. Not mastered yet, mind you. Not exactly fit for the emperor, haha. Anything else you'd have me add?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: That's all? That's what you use your arcane skills for?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hm? Of course not. I'm capable of much more than this.

Bent over, Paper Heron makes a gesture with her right hand. As she does, a line of sharp white Qi wraps around her finger. As she begins moving her finger through the air, the form of a reed plant etches itself into the stone.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: See? It's you! Quite the way to mark the moment, eh?
It doesn't seem to ease her new friend's concerns.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Heron, no! You turned me into a bundle of hay, remember? They'll know it was me.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah! You're right. I'll undo it at once.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: For a moment, I thought that our names might be here for all to see for the next ten thousand years, not mere minutes.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Wait.
She stops Paper Heron's hand with a firm shake of her head.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Leave it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: It'll be a keepsake, like you said. If someone a thousand years from now see it and know I was here ...

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Well, that wouldn't be so bad.
Her voice seems to echo as if coming from some hollow void within her.
Paper Heron studies her young friend. Thoughts flutter across her eyes until she nods and smiles.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Very well. Now stop your fretting.
A set of hurried footsteps comes from afar.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: They're coming. Hush. I'll slip you into my sleeve.
Paper Heron utters an incantation. In an instant, Mayfly transforms into a paper figure that she slips into her sleeve.

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: Chief Chéng, she's in there.
The two constables open the cell door, barging inside before coming to a stop directly in front of Paper Heron.

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: You claimed to be a Daoist. Where's your certificate?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Here.
The chief takes her certificate and furrows his brow as he reads. He looks from the certificate to Paper Heron and then to the mule.

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: Issued in the Hongwu era? That's over 100 years ago!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Daoists cultivate themselves for longevity. It's only natural she looks younger than she is.
Yáng Wǔ stares at Paper Heron in wide-mouthed disbelief, but the chief has already moved on from those minor details.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: What is your relationship with the plant spirit that was revealed at the gate?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I have no relationship with her at all. We simply happened to be in line at the same time. I didn't even know she was a Yao.
He does not reply but glances up at Paper Heron, then back at the certificate.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Oh! Do I need a certificate for my mule too?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Is your mule a Daoist?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: No.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Then no.

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: Heh. What kind of interrogation is this?
Completing his check with a resigned nod, Chéng Héguāng returns the certificate to Paper Heron.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Certificate's clear. You may go, but don't make any more trouble, or there will be consequences.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Not to worry, officer. I always keep to the straight and narrow.
He shifts his focus from the woman to the nearby cell.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Where's the plant spirit?

items.speaker: Yang Wu
items.text: In the next cell. Hasn't turned back to her human form yet. I think she's playing dead.
As the two men walk over to the next cell, Paper Heron leads her mule out from the dark, damp place.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Here we are, free once more. Feeling alright?
Finding a quiet spot, the paper figure drifts from Paper Heron's sleeve and, in a puff of smoke, returns Mayfly to her familiar form.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Didn't I say that all would work out just fine?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hmm. Mmm.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: It's not much fun being a piece of paper. I couldn't see or hear much of anything, and my body was so flat.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I think I heard something about the Hongwu era?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Haha, my Daoist certificate, long expired. Fortunate for us, the constable was too dull to notice.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Tell me, what do you plan to do in town? I hope our delay has not brought you trouble.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Well, ah, oh right, are you hungry, Heron?
She points to a nearby stall. The street has swelled with people, and as the crowd grows, the stall owners call out all the louder for attention.
A line has formed around a set of steaming bamboo baskets. Mayfly slips into the crowd of eager customers.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *sigh* I haven't eaten since this morning. I should've had that clear soup.

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: Here's your sweet olive cake, fresh from the steamer.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Thank you. *sniff* Smells divine.
She cannot wait and takes a bite. A soft, sweet scent fills the air, and a sigh of pure contentment follows.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Mm, mm. It's ... It's so good.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Really? It's only cake.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I can't help it. It's sweet, tender, chewy. You must try it.
She smiles and hands Paper Heron a sweet olive cake, still hot to the touch. Paper Heron looks it over, then delicately lifts it to her mouth.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: So? So? Isn't it wonderful?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mmm. Hmm. The texture is quite remarkable.
She chews with effort, searching for the vaunted taste within.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mmm. I think ...

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What? What??
She watches Mayfly as she chews, each bite meeting waves of rapture, and attempts to mimic her delight. Somehow, the act of imitation seems to conjure the promised flavors.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I think it's sweet, and it grows sweeter and sweeter the more I chew.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Right?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mmm. It's good, delicious. I must get some more. Mm. Here, eat up, Mayfly.

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: You two must be visitors. Are you here for the fair?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: *burp* That's right. Heard it would be quite the spectacle.

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: It certainly will be. And thanks to that rumor, business is going great this year.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: What makes this year so special, hm?

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: Well, many religious sects have flourished in Zhu County recently, each one claiming to bring longevity to their followers. All just tall tales, of course.

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: Only this time is different. Well, it's hearsay. But many think the reason the fair is so busy this year is that one of the sponsors found a true immortal.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I heard that too. My friend said her friend's grandfather, who'd been buried, suddenly came home alive, saying he was enlightened by an immortal in Zhu County.

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: And they say tonight's opera is in fact an opening ceremony for the immortal's sect. They've even widened the stage.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah. Sounds impressive.

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: And not just that. Have you noticed the constables? I've never seen them so nervous. I'd say ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm. But these are mere fancies. Is there nothing we can see with our own eyes?

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: Certainly, the Stilted Parade.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Oh, the Stilted Parade.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: The event you mentioned on the way here, isn't it?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Yes! I heard it's great fun. Where can we see it?

items.speaker: Stall Owner I
items.text: Right behind you.
The stall owner closes the steamer and slips back into the storefront.
It's only now that they realize how quiet the street had become. Not a soul in sight, until a strange, dense bank of perfumed air rolls past them.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Hmm?
